government.note: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy. The Prime Minister heads the government and depends on the confidence of the House of Commons; the monarch's role is largely ceremonial. National referendums are held only when Parliament passes an act for one (for example 2011 and 2016). The Fixed-term Parliaments Act 2011 fixed election dates until the Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act 2022 replaced it.

system.note: 659 single-member constituencies on 1 January 2000 (646 from 2005, 650 from 2010). seats_2000 is the 1997 result adjusted for floor crossings to 1 January 2000: Peter Temple-Morris (Con to Lab via independent, 1997-98), Tommy Graham (Lab to independent, 1998), Dennis Canavan (Lab to independent, 1999) and Shaun Woodward (Con to Lab, 18 December 1999). All nine by-elections from 1997 to 1999 were holds, and Ceredigion was not vacated until 10 January 2000. 'others' is the Speaker, Betty Boothroyd; the independents are Martin Bell, Tommy Graham and Dennis Canavan. The two Sinn Fein MPs do not take their seats.

system.note: Appointed life peers, Church of England bishops and (from the House of Lords Act 1999 until 2026) 92 excepted hereditary peers, 75 of them elected by party group (42 Conservative, 28 Crossbench, 3 Liberal Democrat, 2 Labour) and 15 by the whole House. Members have no fixed term. The House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 removed the remaining hereditary peers.

chambers.review_note: 669 is the membership in March 2000 (House of Lords Annual Report 1999-2000, quoted on Wikipedia); the exact figure on 1 January 2000 was not found. The party/group breakdown (Conservative, Labour, Liberal Democrat, Crossbench, bishops, others) for early 2000 could not be fetched (House of Commons Library Research Paper 00/61 was unreachable), so all seats are recorded as 'appointed'. Replace with the group breakdown from that paper.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from 1997 general election UK-wide vote shares: Labour 43.2% (split 30.0 Third Way 'New Labour' / 13.2 social democrat), Conservative 30.7% (22.0 liberal conservative / 8.7 traditional conservative), Liberal Democrats 16.8% plus Alliance 0.2% (social liberal), Referendum Party 2.6% plus UKIP 0.3% (right populist), SNP 2.0% + Plaid Cymru 0.5% + Sinn Fein 0.4% (regionalist/nationalist), UUP 0.8% (traditional conservative), SDLP 0.6% (social democrat), DUP 0.3% (national conservative), Greens 0.2% plus others (green), Socialist Labour 0.2% and others (democratic socialist), BNP 0.1% (ethno-nationalist), independents, the Speaker and minor parties about 0.8% (big tent). Splits within Labour and the Conservatives are gameplay estimates.
